title: Microsoft Teams: choose the institution type in the Teams for Education Policy Wizard
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, wizard behaviour, licensing background and documented navigation are supported. One minor consistency issue remains: the checklist asks administrators to check educator and staff policies, but the controls table covers only institution type selection.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 402185 describes administrators selecting their institution's tenant type in the policy wizard.
claims.quote: Admins can now select tenant type for their institution from the policy wizard.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the tenant type can be changed later through the wizard.
claims.quote: This setting can be changed anytime from the wizard.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2024.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2024"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) and does not list other clouds.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platforms are Desktop, Mac and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Mac", "Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The wizard's educational institution type options are Primary or Secondary and Higher education.
claims.quote: Select your educational institution type (**Primary or Secondary** or **Higher education**), and then select **Next**.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The wizard adjusts students' Global (Org-wide default) policy definitions according to institution type.
claims.quote: The wizard adjusts the Global (Org-wide default) policy definition of each policy area covered by the wizard with new default settings that are appropriate to keep your students safe.

claims.claim: The wizard creates custom policy definitions for educators and staff.
claims.quote: The wizard creates a set of custom policy definitions for each policy area covered by the wizard with settings tailored to the needs of educators and staff.

claims.claim: The wizard assigns the educator and staff custom policies to groups selected by the administrator.
claims.quote: Then, it assigns the policy definitions to the group of educators and staff that you choose.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The administrator can select up to three educator and staff groups.
claims.quote: You can select up to three groups.

claims.claim: The student policy areas are Teams, Meeting, Live events, App setup, App permission, Messaging and Calling.
claims.quote:
Teams policy
Meeting policy
Live events policy
App setup policy
App permission policy
Messaging policy
Calling policy

claims.claim: The five educator and staff custom policy areas are Teams, Meeting, Live events, Messaging and Calling.
claims.quote:
Teams policy | Primary or Secondary Educators and Staff - Teams
Meeting policy | Primary or Secondary Educators and Staff - Meeting
Live events policy | Primary or Secondary Educators and Staff - Live events
Messaging policy | Primary or Secondary Educators and Staff - Messaging
Calling policy

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Why it matters
claims.claim: Changing only the institution type applies the new type's Global policy definitions to students.
claims.quote: Change only the educational institution type | - **Students**: The Global (Org-wide default) policy definitions based on the new educational institution type are applied to students.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Why it matters
claims.claim: Changing only the institution type creates and assigns new custom policy definitions to the educator and staff groups.
claims.quote: A set of custom policy definitions based on the new educational institution type is created and assigned to the educators and staff groups.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Changing institution type removes the previous type's custom policy definitions from the educator and staff groups.
claims.quote: The custom policy definitions created for the previous educational institution type are removed from the educators and staff groups.

claims.claim: The wizard's Learn page does not say when institution type selection was added.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams for Education Policy Wizard" cost meter default Apply data institution type added. Read easy-policy-setup-edu in full; it documents selecting and changing type but gives no introduction date.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: After the wizard has run, education defaults for new Teams features are automatically added to Global policies without administrator intervention.
claims.quote: whenever a new feature is added to Teams, the appropriate EDU relevant default value of the policy for that feature will be automatically added to the Global (Org-wide default) without requiring any admin intervention.

claims.claim: The sources do not say this wizard changes existing policies if nobody runs it.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams for Education Policy Wizard" cost meter default Apply data institution type added. Read the roadmap and easy-policy-setup-edu: policy application is described as occurring when the wizard runs, with Apply.

claims.claim: The feature description documents no new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams for Education Policy Wizard" cost meter default Apply data institution type added. Read roadmap description and easy-policy-setup-edu, including policy tables; they describe policy configuration, not a new data-access mechanism.

claims.claim: The wizard's policies govern available Teams features and what students can share.
claims.quote: you can use policies to control who can use private chat and private calling, who can schedule meetings, and what content types can be shared.

claims.claim: Learn describes student policies as more restrictive than educator and staff policies.
claims.quote: Policies for students need to be more restrictive to reduce their risk of receiving inappropriate levels of access. Educators and staff need a separate set of policies that can be more permissive

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Existing student direct and group policy assignments must be removed for the wizard's Global policies to take effect.
claims.quote: Remove all existing direct assignments and group assignments from your students so that the Global (Org-wide default) policy definition applied by the wizard takes effect.

claims.claim: The wizard assigns educator and staff group policies at ranking 1, the highest ranking.
claims.quote: the wizard assigns policies to your educators and staff group using a group assignment ranking of 1, which is the highest ranking.

claims.claim: An existing policy in the same policy area on a selected educator and staff group is moved to a lower ranking.
claims.quote: If your educators and staff group has an existing policy of the same policy area assigned to it, that existing policy is moved to a lower ranking and the policy assigned by the wizard takes effect.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Conflicting direct assignments override the wizard's educator and staff group policies and must be removed for those policies to take effect.
claims.quote: Remove any conflicting direct assignments for your educators and staff so that the custom policy definition created by the wizard takes effect.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Initial policy application is admin-opt-in: the administrator selects Apply to apply the wizard's changes.
claims.quote: Select **Apply** to apply your changes.

claims.claim: The wizard starts automatically for someone new to Teams.
claims.quote: If you're new to Teams, the wizard automatically starts.

claims.claim: Applying the wizard's changes may take a few minutes, with Global definitions immediately applied to students.
claims.quote: This may take a few minutes to complete.The Global (Org-wide default) policy definitions are immediately applied to students.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Custom policy assignment to educator and staff group members can take a few hours depending on group size.
claims.quote: For your educators and staff, it could take a few hours for the custom policies to be assigned to each member of the groups you selected, depending on the size of the groups.

claims.claim: Learn describes no mechanism for carrying edits to previous custom policies into the new policies when institution type changes.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Education Policy Wizard institution type PowerShell Graph API tenant type Quick setup Change default role licensing. Read easy-policy-setup-edu, Make changes in the wizard: it describes creating new definitions and removing previous definitions, not migrating edits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Teams for Education requires an Education license in the Microsoft 365 tenant.
claims.quote:
## Prerequisites for Microsoft Teams for Education

- An Education license in your Microsoft 365 tenant

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft lists Teams as part of the free Microsoft 365 A1 for Students SKU.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams is part of the free Microsoft 365 A1 for Students SKU.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The wizard page states no separate wizard-specific licence requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams for Education Policy Wizard" "role" "license". Read easy-policy-setup-edu, teams-edu-licensing and baseline-apps-teams-what-is-teams; the wizard page names no separate wizard-specific licence.

claims.claim: The wizard page publishes no meter for the wizard.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams for Education Policy Wizard" cost meter default Apply data institution type added. Read easy-policy-setup-edu and teams-edu-licensing; the wizard page publishes no billing meter.

claims.claim: The wizard's Learn page names no required administrator role.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams for Education Policy Wizard" "role" "license". Read easy-policy-setup-edu in full: no required role is named. The role in Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration concerns that cmdlet, not the wizard.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The first-run wizard is reached in Microsoft Teams admin center through Home > Easy policy setup for a safe learning environment > Quick setup, with institution type chosen next.
claims.quote:
go to **Home**, and then in the **Easy policy setup for a safe learning environment** tile, select **Quick setup**.
2. Select your educational institution type (**Primary or Secondary** or **Higher education**)

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API operation for the wizard's initial institution type selection is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "institution type" "Set-Cs"; site:learn.microsoft.com graph education settings institution type policy wizard API. Read easy-policy-setup-edu, Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration and Graph education-overview; no initial type-selection call.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The wizard can be rerun to change institution type through Microsoft Teams admin center > Home > Easy policy setup for a safe learning environment > Change.
claims.quote:
go to **Home**, and then in the **Easy policy setup for a safe learning environment** tile, select **Change**.
2. From here, continue through each page of the wizard to make your changes. You can change your institution type

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API control to change the wizard's institution type is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "institution type" "Set-Cs"; site:learn.microsoft.com graph education settings institution type policy wizard API. Read easy-policy-setup-edu, Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration and Graph education-overview; no institution-type change operation.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration has no institution type parameter in its documented syntax.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "institution type" "Set-Cs". Read Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration syntax and all parameters: ParentGuardianPreferredContactMethod, UpdateParentInformation, EduGenerativeAIEnhancements, Identity, WhatIf, Confirm and common parameters; no institution type.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included under the Teams for Education product licence rather than a documented separate wizard entitlement.
claims.quote:
## Prerequisites for Microsoft Teams for Education

- An Education license in your Microsoft 365 tenant
- Enable Microsoft Teams in the Microsoft Admin Center

claims.claim: Learn instructs administrators without educator and staff groups to create a group and rerun the wizard.
claims.quote: If you don't have any groups set up yet for your educators and staff, create a group, and then rerun the wizard.

claims.claim: The wizard includes a review step before Apply.
claims.quote:
4. Review your selections.
5. Select **Apply** to apply your changes.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends checking Message Center for new Teams features, policies and settings.
claims.quote: But do check the Message Center (in the Microsoft 365 admin center) frequently to stay up to date on new features and their policies and policy settings in Teams.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks administrators to check is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Check the educators and staff policies a few hours after applying; controls table: Institution type chosen on the first run of the wizard; Institution type changed after the wizard has run.
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout bullet 'Check the educators and staff policies a few hours after applying, as Learn says assignment can take that long.' It asks for a policy check not represented by either institution-type control row.
